6.text: I was told that the application of cold water to the head of a shaman

7.text: in the very heat of his performance would suddenly bring his inspiration to

8.text: an end. Therefore sometimes, during the ceremonials, if some performer is

9.text: practising too long, or seems to be excited to a somewhat dangerous pitch,

10.text: his neighbors may sprinkle him with water in order to bring him back to himself.

11.text: The performance itself is considered as a recovery from illness. The

12.text: same shaman who was nervous before the performance regains after it his

13.text: self-possession, and looks really as if he were braced up by some strong tonic.

14.text: Even the physical fatigue is in most cases quite unnoticeable. “Why should

15.text: I feel fatigued?” asked a Chukchee shaman in regard to this subject. “I do

16.text: nothing. The ‘spirits’ make all the exertion.” Accordingly, the former,

17.text: constraint gives place to an exaggerated self-conceit, and even the most “bashful”

18.text: of the young shamans are wont, after a performance, to magnify their own

24.text: SHAMANISTIC PERFORMANCE IN THE INNER ROOM. — The typical shamanistic

25.text: performance is carried out in the following manner. After the evening meal

26.text: is finished and the kettles and trays are removed to the outer tent, all the

27.text: people who wish to be present at the séance enter the inner room, which is

28.text: carefully closed for the night. Among the Reindeer Chukchee, the inner room

29.text: is especially small, and its narrow space causes much inconvenience to the

30.text: audience, which is packed together in a tight and most uncomfortable manner.

31.text: The Maritime Chukchee have more room, and may listen to the voices of

32.text: the spirits with more ease and freedom. The shaman sits on the “master’s

33.text: place,” near the back wall; and even in the most limited sleeping-room, some

34.text: free space must be left around him. The drum is carefully looked over, its

35.text: head tightened, and, if it is much shrunken, it is moistened with urine and

36.text: hung up for a short time over the lamp to dry. The shaman sometimes

37.text: occupies more than an hour in this process, before he is satisfied with the

38.text: drum. To have more freedom in his movements, the shaman usually takes

39.text: off his fur shirt, and remains quite naked down to the waist. He often
